title: The Tree of Life and the Vine of Wisdom
english: In the new covenant, the testimonies taken from the book of the Psalms are set forth as having been spoken by the Holy Spirit. Paul, having taken a chapter from the ninety-fourth Psalm in the epistle to the Hebrews, writes that it was announced by the Holy Spirit, saying, 'As the Holy Spirit says: If today you hear his voice...' (Hebrews 3:7), and the following. To this, Peter, the forerunner of the apostles, also says in the Acts of the apostles according to the pattern: 'It was necessary for the scripture to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit foretold through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who became a guide to those who seize Jesus' (Acts 1:16), and the following, having said a few words, he brought forward: 'For it is written in the book of Psalms: Let his habitation become a desert, and let him not dwell in it; and let another take his oversight' (Psalm 69:25). It is nothing foreign if the apostles write these things, especially since the Savior is sealing these things. For a memory having occurred in the Gospel of the ninety-first Psalm at the beginning, sounding thus: 'The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet' (Psalm 109:1), the Pharisees were eager to ask if David, in the Holy Spirit, says Christ is Lord, how he is his son. If, therefore, the Psalms contain spiritual meanings, it was not by chance that they were composed in their scripture.

2 Ps 1,1 It is the way of sinners for the devil to say, in which the one having become [one] should not remain, following the deceptive teaching: 'Resist the devil and he will flee from you' (James 4:7). He who does not stand in this way will come to the one saying, 'I am the way' (John 14:6), and if, having become [one], running according to the purpose, he will win the prize. 3 Ps 1,3 ab For how must the one testified to by the things said, as being wise, not resemble wisdom? For someone resembles one bestowing such a quality, or does not the righteous resemble the just...

Eternal and holy in holiness; if this is so, then the wise man is also wise in wisdom. Having approached and broken being away from it, the wise man becomes like it, according to what was said by the Savior: 'It is sufficient for the disciple that he become as his teacher, and the servant as his lord' (Matt 10:25).

And he who becomes like the tree of life is planted in paradise to be with it; thus it is heard of what is written in Isaiah from the face of God: 'The days of the people of my God shall be as the days of the wood of life' (Isa 66:19). This being true, since the wood of life is eternal, it joins and shares in the passion of Him; thus the likeness makes us grow together in the wood, so that we may be made branches and shoots to bring forth divine fruit. For the wood of life is said to be a true vine toward those becoming imitators through goodness: 'I am the true vine; you are the branches; my Father is the gardener; every branch abiding in me, he prunes it, so that it may bear more fruit' (John 15:1, 2, 5).

But also, the mystical and spiritual understanding of the Scriptures is a fruit of the wood planted by the watercourses (this is the wisdom of God), and the ready words are leaves covering the said fruit, intended to do the proper work in guarding the fruits and becoming food for the most pure men, those called simple like cattle, according to: 'You will save men and cattle, Lord' (Ps 35:6).

For if they desire to be in the deficiency of dust through impiety and to bear the image of the swine, similarly they are swept away from the face of the earth by the most meager dust, being scattered there by the evil wind.
